title: Parent College Visit Checklist
subtitle: Collect evidence. Understand costs. Decide together.
sections: Before the visit
Write the student's two or three branch interests and your practical budget.
Read the exact programme syllabus and current official admission notice.
Ask for evidence
Who teaches core subjects, and how do students get help?
Can ordinary students use functioning labs, computers and the library?
What support exists for language, accessibility, wellbeing and grievances?
Ask current students independently about learning, travel and hostel conditions.
Understand the cost and outcomes
Add tuition, compulsory fees, hostel/transport, food, learning access and travel.
Check scholarship award/renewal conditions; do not count unconfirmed support.
Read written withdrawal/refund terms and keep receipts.
For placement claims, ask the branch/year, unique students, denominator and roles.
After the visit
Record the strongest evidence, the main trade-off and one unanswered question.
Compare at least two actual college-and-course options with the student.

title: Seven-Day Branch Exploration
subtitle: Make a shortlist through small activities, not hype.
sections: Day 1 - Start with questions
Write three problems you would like to understand or improve. Pick two or three branches to investigate.
Days 2 to 4 - Try the work
Do one small activity per branch: paper, simulation or safe supervised work is enough.
Record what interested you and what was difficult; lack of access is not lack of ability.
Day 5 - Compare actual subjects
Read the first two years of each shortlisted college syllabus. Look up unfamiliar terms.
Day 6 - Talk to people
Ask a current student and practitioner what they study or do in an ordinary week.
Day 7 - Reflect and compare
Would you spend another hour learning this? What evidence is still missing?
Compare costs, teaching/lab access and practical constraints with your family.

title: Branch Comparison Worksheet
subtitle: Compare actual options. Unknown means investigate.
sections: Use evidence, not an automatic score
Try an activity, inspect the syllabus and collect teaching/lab evidence.
A serious cost or access constraint can outweigh several small advantages.
